clusters.name: Skin layers
clusters.fact: Skin has three main layers: the epidermis forms the outer barrier, the dermis supports glands, follicles and sensation, and the fatty hypodermis cushions and insulates.

epidermis.text: The outermost skin layer, made largely of keratin-producing cells that create a protective, water-resistant surface.

dermis.text: The thick middle skin layer containing connective tissue, blood vessels, nerves, hair follicles and glands.

hypodermis.text: The fatty layer beneath the dermis that cushions deeper tissues, stores energy and helps insulate the body.

clusters.name: Accessory structures
clusters.fact: Hair, nails and skin glands are accessory structures of the integumentary system: they protect surfaces and release substances such as sweat and sebum.

hair.text: Keratin-based filaments that grow from follicles and help with protection, insulation and light-touch sensation.

nails.text: Hard keratin plates that protect the sensitive tips of the fingers and toes and assist with fine manipulation.

sweat glands.text: Skin glands that release sweat; eccrine glands open onto the skin surface, while apocrine glands open into hair follicles.

sebaceous glands.text: Glands, usually connected to hair follicles, that secrete oily sebum to help lubricate skin and hair.

clusters.name: System functions
clusters.fact: The integumentary system protects the body, regulates temperature, detects sensations and uses sunlight to help synthesize vitamin D.

barrier protection.text: The skin's physical and chemical defenses against injury, microbes, ultraviolet radiation and excessive water loss.

temperature regulation.text: Keeping internal temperature within a workable range through mechanisms including sweating, changes in skin blood flow and insulation.

sensation.text: Skin receptors and nerve endings detect touch, pressure, pain, itch, heat and cold.

vitamin D synthesis.text: Ultraviolet light begins a chemical process in the skin that allows the body to produce vitamin D.

bridges.fact: Keratin bridges skin layers and accessory structures: keratin-producing cells strengthen the epidermis, and hardened keratin forms the main structural material of hair and nails.

info.text: A tough structural protein produced by skin cells and used throughout the epidermis, hair and nails.

bridges.fact: Sweating bridges accessory structures and system functions: sweat glands release fluid onto the skin, and its evaporation removes heat to help regulate body temperature.

info.text: The release of sweat onto the skin, especially from eccrine glands, where evaporation can cool the body.
